t: Which of the following is a consequential-loss (business interruption) type of engineering cover?
o: Machinery Breakdown
Contractors' Plant and Machinery
Machinery Loss of Profits
Boiler and Pressure Plant
e: MLOP, ALOP and DOS are consequential covers that depend on a material damage policy; MBD, CPM and BPP are material damage covers.

t: A CAR policy's period includes a maintenance period only when:
o: The contract value exceeds ₹10 crore
Automatically in every CAR policy
The principal is a government body
The contract provides for a defects liability period and the maintenance cover is opted for at additional premium
e: Maintenance cover is an optional extension matching the defects liability obligation in the contract.

t: Which of the following expenses is NOT payable under a basic CAR policy unless a specific extension is purchased?
o: Cost of materials used in reinstating damaged works
Normal wages of workmen engaged in repairs
Overtime, night work and express freight on materials
Cost of replacing damaged formwork included in the sum insured
e: Expediting expenses are extra costs beyond normal reinstatement and need an extension with its own limit.

t: Under a CAR policy, which of the following is correct regarding sub-contractors?
o: They cannot be covered under the main contractor's CAR policy
They must take separate CAR policies by law
They are usually included as insureds for their work on the site, and the insurer waives subrogation against them to that extent
Their work is covered only under Section II
e: Naming sub-contractors avoids recovery actions among parties working on the same project and gives them cover for their portion of works.

t: A contractor building a 10 km canal has a CAR policy. A landslide damages 500 metres of lining with a loss of ₹18 lakh; AOG excess is 10% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹1 lakh. Debris removal costs ₹3 lakh and the debris extension limit is ₹2 lakh. Total payable:
e: Lining: ₹18 lakh − ₹1.8 lakh = ₹16.2 lakh; debris limited to ₹2 lakh; total ₹18,20,000.

t: A contractor's CAR policy contains a limit of indemnity under Section II of ₹50 lakh any one accident and ₹1 crore in aggregate. Three separate accidents result in third-party awards of ₹40 lakh, ₹60 lakh and ₹30 lakh. The insurer's total liability is:
e: Accident-wise limits: ₹40 lakh, ₹50 lakh (capped) and ₹30 lakh = ₹1.2 crore, but the aggregate limit restricts total liability to ₹1 crore.

t: Which of the following statements about CAR cover for 'cessation of work' is correct?
o: Stoppage of work extends the policy period free of cost
Cover continues unchanged regardless of stoppage
The policy automatically lapses on the first day of stoppage
If work is interrupted for a prolonged period the insurer must be informed and cover may be restricted or terms revised
e: Idle sites present different hazards; the policy requires notice of material changes such as cessation of work.

t: Which of the following would NOT normally be included in an EAR sum insured?
o: Cost of the machinery and equipment
Freight and insurance charges to site
Customs duty on imported items
Land cost of the project site
e: Land is not exposed to erection perils; all costs of the plant in its erected state, including freight and duty, are included.

t: Under an EAR policy, loss of or damage to erection plant and equipment (cranes, winches) used by the erector is covered:
o: Automatically, as part of the plant being erected
Never, under any circumstances
Only if declared and insured as a separate item or section at an additional premium
Only after the testing period
e: Erection tools and plant are a separate exposure and must be specified; otherwise a CPM policy is needed.

t: A refinery EAR policy has a sum insured of ₹900 crore, a project period of 36 months and a testing period of 8 weeks. The rate is 0.25% for the basic period with an additional 0.05% for the extended testing. The total premium before GST is:
e: Total rate 0.30% on ₹900 crore = ₹2,70,00,000.

t: Under the Insurance Act, 1938, the provisions on surveyors and loss assessors are contained in Section:
o: 64VB
64UM
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64UM deals with licensing of surveyors and the requirement of survey reports; 64VB is premium in advance, 45 non-contestability and 41 rebating.

t: Which of the following is a standard exclusion under an EAR policy relating to the contractor?
o: Loss due to carelessness of erection workers
Loss or damage due to wilful act or wilful negligence of the insured or his representatives
Loss due to failure of lifting tackle
Loss due to faulty erection by workmen
e: Wilful acts are excluded under all engineering policies; ordinary negligence and faulty erection are covered as accidental causes.

t: Which of the following items is usually rated separately under an EAR policy because of its higher hazard?
o: Office furniture at site
Civil engineering works forming part of the project
Testing period and AOG perils
The contractor's vehicles
e: Testing and AOG perils carry additional rates and higher excesses; civil works are included at the project rate.

t: Which of the following is a correct statement about CPM policies?
o: The policy covers the machine only while being operated by the owner
Hired machines cannot be insured under CPM
The policy can cover machines hired by the contractor, with the owner's interest noted
The policy covers only machines less than 2 years old
e: CPM can cover owned or hired plant; the hirer's contractual responsibility makes this cover important.

t: Which of the following perils is excluded under CPM?
o: Damage caused by total or partial immersion in tidal waters, unless specifically covered
Overturning due to soft ground
Collision with another machine on site
Fire due to a hydraulic oil leak
e: Immersion in tidal waters and work on waterborne platforms are standard exclusions; the other perils are covered external accidents.

t: A tower crane insured under CPM collapses because the contractor loaded it beyond its safe working load during a lift. The claim is:
o: Payable in full
Excluded, as loss due to overloading or tests involving abnormal conditions is not covered
Payable at 50%
Payable if the operator was certified
e: Overloading beyond rated capacity is a standard CPM exclusion.

t: Which of the following is covered under MBD in respect of electrical machinery?
o: Damage by flood water in the cable trench
Damage caused by lightning striking the transformer yard
Damage caused by fire in the switch room
Damage to insulation caused by excessive voltage, short circuit or arcing
e: Electrical breakdown causes are MBD perils; lightning, fire and flood are fire-policy perils and are excluded.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under an MLOP policy the annual gross profit is ₹2.4 crore, the indemnity period 12 months and the time excess 14 days. A covered breakdown stops production for 44 days. Ignoring savings, the loss payable is approximately:
o: ₹28.9 lakh
₹9.2 lakh
₹19.7 lakh
₹24.0 lakh
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Only 30 days (44 less the 14-day time excess) are indemnifiable; ₹2.4 crore ÷ 365 × 30 ≈ ₹19.7 lakh.

t: Which of the following best describes the treatment of 'tests and experiments' under MBD?
o: Damage during normal operational tests is covered, but damage from experiments or tests involving abnormal stress is excluded
All tests are excluded
All experiments are covered
Tests are covered only for new machines
e: Routine operational checks are part of normal working; abnormal tests and overloading are excluded.

t: A paper mill's refiner is insured under MBD. It fails because of a casting defect in the housing supplied with the machine 8 years ago, outside any warranty. The claim is:
o: Excluded, as defects in material are never covered
Covered only if the supplier is Indian
Covered, as defects in casting and material are insured MBD perils when no supplier or manufacturer is legally liable
Excluded, as the machine is more than 5 years old
e: MBD specifically covers defects in material, casting, design and workmanship; the exclusion applies only where the maker/supplier is liable.

t: An induction furnace insured under MBD for ₹1.2 crore suffers damage; repair cost ₹30 lakh, which includes ₹6 lakh for the refractory lining. The policy excess is 1% of the sum insured. Amount payable:
e: Refractory linings are excluded as consumables: ₹30 lakh − ₹6 lakh = ₹24 lakh; less excess ₹1.2 lakh = ₹22,80,000.

t: A stand-by diesel generator that is not in regular use is proposed for MBD. The underwriter would normally:
o: Decline cover for idle machinery
Accept the machine, as MBD covers machinery at rest as well as at work, possibly at a reduced rate for stand-by equipment
Insist on an EAR policy
Accept only for fire perils
e: MBD applies to machinery whether working or idle; stand-by plant has lower exposure and may be rated accordingly.

t: Which of the following is the typical structure of a BPP policy's cover?
o: Only damage to the boiler itself
Loss of profit due to boiler failure
Only third-party liability
Damage to the boiler/pressure plant, damage to the insured's surrounding property, and third-party liability for bodily injury and property damage
e: BPP has three heads of cover: the plant, surrounding property and legal liability to third parties.

t: Which of the following statements regarding BPP is INCORRECT?
o: Boilers must be inspected and certified under the Boilers Act for cover to be granted
Failure of individual tubes in a boiler is excluded
Flue-gas explosion in the furnace is covered under BPP
Explosion caused by shortage of water can be covered
e: Flue gas explosion is a fire-policy peril and is excluded under BPP; the other statements are correct.

t: A boiler insured under BPP for ₹60 lakh collapses due to crushing stress of steam pressure. Repair cost is ₹15 lakh, of which ₹2 lakh relates to replacement of individual tubes that failed independently, and the excess is ₹25,000. Amount payable:
e: Individual tube failure is excluded: ₹15 lakh − ₹2 lakh = ₹13 lakh; less excess ₹25,000 = ₹12,75,000.

t: A proposal for MBD on a 25-year-old rolling mill with a poor maintenance record is received. The appropriate underwriting response is:
o: Accept at standard rate
Decline or accept only after a risk inspection, with loading and a higher excess
Accept with free testing cover
Accept on first-loss basis without inspection
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Age and maintenance are key MBD rating factors; an inspection report determines whether the risk is acceptable and on what terms.

t: Under an EEI policy, the equipment is covered:
o: Only while in operation
While at work or at rest, or being dismantled for cleaning or overhauling, at the insured premises
Only during office hours
Only while under maintenance contract
e: Like MBD, EEI covers the equipment at the premises whether in use or idle, including during cleaning and overhaul.

t: Which of the following is a correct statement about EEI partial loss settlement?
o: Repairs are paid without depreciation, including dismantling, re-erection and ordinary freight
Repairs are paid after deducting depreciation of 10% per year
Only the labour cost is paid
Only the cost of parts is paid
e: EEI partial losses are paid on repair cost without depreciation, subject to the sum insured and excess; depreciation applies only in a total loss.

t: Which of the following extensions can be added to an EEI policy?
o: Cover for mechanical breakdown of a steam turbine
Cover for employee dishonesty
Cover for loss of profit due to a fire
Cover for the cost of hiring a substitute computer (increased cost of working under Section III)
e: ICOW is Section III of the EEI policy; the other covers belong to MBD, fire LOP and fidelity guarantee respectively.

t: An EEI policy covers a bank's servers with Section III ICOW at ₹50,000 per day, an indemnity period of 3 months and a time excess of 2 days. After an insured surge, the bank hires stand-by servers for 12 days at ₹60,000 per day. The ICOW claim payable is:
e: Only 10 days are indemnifiable (12 − 2) and the cover is limited to ₹50,000 per day: 10 × ₹50,000 = ₹5,00,000.

t: A DOS claim arises when the compressor breaks down but the stock is saved because the stand-by compressor is started within an hour. The DOS insurer:
o: Must pay the full sum insured
Pays 10% of the sum insured as inconvenience
Pays nothing for the stock, since no deterioration occurred, although the MBD policy may respond for the compressor repair
Pays the cost of running the stand-by
e: DOS indemnifies actual deterioration of stock; absence of deterioration means no DOS loss, though the machinery damage is an MBD matter.

t: For a seasonal potato cold storage, the DOS policy is normally issued:
o: For the storage season with the sum insured and premium reflecting the stock build-up and decline
For 5 years at a time
Only for 24 hours
Without any sum insured
e: Potato storages operate seasonally (roughly March to November), so cover and declarations follow the season and stock pattern.

t: Which of the following is a typical DOS exclusion relating to the cold storage operator?
o: Deterioration due to breakdown of the insured machinery
Deterioration due to the insured's failure to keep proper temperature records or to maintain the plant as required
Deterioration due to escape of refrigerant
Deterioration due to accidental failure of the public power supply when the extension is held
e: Breach of the conditions regarding maintenance and records relieves the insurer; the other items are insured perils.

t: Which of the following is a CECR exclusion?
o: Storm damage to a flyover
Damage to a canal lining caused by gradual seepage and normal silting
Riot damage to a toll plaza structure
Earthquake damage to a tunnel portal
e: Gradual processes such as seepage, silting and scour over time are excluded; sudden named perils are covered.

t: A municipal corporation's completed water treatment plant includes civil tanks and pumping machinery. The correct combination of covers is:
o: CECR for everything including pumps
CAR for everything
EAR for everything
CECR for the civil structures and MBD for the pumps and electrical machinery
e: Each asset is placed under the appropriate operational cover: CECR for structures and MBD for machinery.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which of the following is the basic precondition for an ALOP claim?
o: Delay in the project due to any cause
Admission of a material damage claim under the CAR/EAR policy and a resulting delay in commencement of business beyond the time excess
Delay of more than 12 months
A liquidated damages claim by the principal
e: ALOP follows the material damage policy; without an admitted MD claim there is no ALOP claim.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under ALOP, an interest-only cover is sometimes arranged for the project financier. In this case the sum insured represents:
o: The full project cost
The contractor's margin
The interest on project loans payable for the indemnity period
The net profit after tax
e: Financiers' interest can be insured on a debt-service basis, which is simpler than projecting gross profit for a new project.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
o: 15 days
30 days
45 days
60 days
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: In an MLOP claim, the shortage in turnover is computed by comparing:
o: Actual turnover during the indemnity period with standard turnover of the corresponding period of the previous year, adjusted for trend
Current turnover with turnover of the first year of the factory
Actual turnover with the sum insured
Turnover with the MBD sum insured
e: As in fire LOP, the standard turnover (adjusted for trends) is the benchmark against which the actual turnover during interruption is measured.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: A factory with MLOP (annual gross profit ₹3.65 crore, rate of gross profit 25%, time excess 7 days) suffers a breakdown. Standard turnover for the 37-day interruption would have been ₹1.5 crore; actual turnover was ₹60 lakh. Ignoring the time excess apportionment and savings, the loss of gross profit is:
e: Shortage in turnover = ₹1.5 crore − ₹60 lakh = ₹90 lakh; at the 25% rate of gross profit the loss is ₹22,50,000.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which of the following is normally NOT covered under MLOP?
o: Loss of gross profit following an insured breakdown of a boiler covered under BPP
Auditor's fees for preparing the claim, if the extension is held
Increase in cost of working to maintain production after an insured breakdown
Loss of gross profit due to fire damage to machinery
e: Fire-related interruption is the domain of fire LOP; MLOP responds only to interruptions caused by MBD/BPP-type damage.

t: Which of the following is normally required from the proposer before an MBD policy is issued on a large plant?
o: A list of machinery with make, year, capacity and sum insured for each item
The owner's income-tax return
The insurer's reinsurance treaty
A fire brigade certificate
e: MBD is itemised; each machine is listed with details enabling item-wise rating and excess.

t: While underwriting an EEI policy for a data centre, the underwriter would attach most importance to:
o: Air-conditioning, power conditioning (UPS), fire protection and maintenance contracts
The number of visitors to the premises
The colour of the server racks
The proximity to a railway station
e: Environmental control, clean power and maintenance determine the frequency of electronic failures and damage.

t: Which of the following is a legitimate reason for an engineering underwriter to require facultative reinsurance?
o: The sum insured exceeds the insurer's retention and treaty capacity for the risk
The proposer is a government company
The policy is for 12 months
The excess is 5% of the claim
e: Large project values beyond treaty limits are placed facultatively; the nature of the proposer or policy period alone does not require it.

t: In detariffed engineering business, a 'bouquet' or discount for a good claims experience is:
o: Prohibited by IRDAI
A matter for the insurer's underwriting policy, provided it is applied consistently and justified by the risk
Fixed at 10% by law
Available only to public sector insurers
e: Insurers price risks under their own board-approved underwriting policies; discounts must be risk-based and not discriminatory.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
o: ₹20 lakh
₹30 lakh
₹50 lakh
₹1 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: Which of the following is a reason an engineering insurer may repudiate a CAR claim?
o: The loss occurred during the monsoon
The loss arose from a cause that originated before the policy commenced or from wilful negligence
The contractor employed daily-wage labour
The claim was intimated by e-mail
e: Pre-inception causes and wilful acts are excluded; the other items are not grounds for repudiation.

t: Under the IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests regulations, if an insurer delays claim payment beyond the prescribed period it must pay interest at:
o: No interest is payable
Bank rate plus 2% from the date the claim became payable
12% simple interest in all cases
The rate fixed by the insured
e: The regulations require interest at 2% above the bank rate for delayed settlement to protect policyholders.

t: Which of the following is correct regarding arbitration under Indian engineering policies?
o: Arbitration is available only for disputes on the quantum of a claim where liability is admitted
Arbitration decides whether liability exists under the policy
Arbitration is compulsory for every claim above ₹1 lakh
Arbitration is conducted by IRDAI
e: The standard arbitration clause applies to disputes on amount only; questions of liability go to the courts or the Ombudsman.

t: An EEI insured reports a theft of two laptops from the premises six weeks after the event, without a police complaint. The insurer may:
o: Pay the claim in full
Decline for breach of the condition requiring immediate notice and a police report for theft losses
Pay 50% of the claim
Pay only if the laptops were new
e: Prompt notice and a police report are conditions for theft claims; late reporting prejudices investigation and recovery.
